How much should you tip for tattoo removal?

At a dedicated removal studio, 15–20% of each session: $30–40 on a $200 session. At a med spa it is optional, around 10–15%. When a doctor or nurse does it in a clinic, no tip is expected.

What makes removal different from almost any other tipped service is that you are paying for a course, not a visit. Most tattoos need 6–12 sessions spaced six to eight weeks or more apart, so a removal can run a year or longer. A $200 session tipped at 17% over eight sessions is about $275 in tips, worth budgeting for alongside the treatment itself.

Studio or clinic, and a course of 6–12 sessions

  • Ink colors: black and dark blue usually respond fastest. Green, light blue, yellow and white often take extra sessions and more careful work. A multi-color piece is a reason to sit at the top of the range.
  • Size and density: a large or heavily saturated tattoo means more passes per session and more cooling and comfort care from the technician.
  • Fading for a cover-up: lightening a tattoo so an artist can cover it usually takes fewer sessions than full removal. Tip each of those sessions the same way.
  • Between-session care: a technician who walks you through blistering, healing and sun protection, and checks how you healed before the next pass, is doing more than the minutes on the clock.

Tattoo removal tipping etiquette

Tip something at every session rather than saving one large amount for the end. Over a year-long course you may not see the same technician for the final visit, and the person who did the hard early sessions should not miss out.

How fast a tattoo fades depends on the ink, your skin and your immune system, not on the technician. Judge the tip on how you were treated in the chair, not on how quickly the tattoo is disappearing.

Card tips are routine at removal studios and med spas, so cash or card are both fine.

Frequently asked questions

How much should you tip for tattoo removal?
At dedicated tattoo removal studios, tip 15–20% of the session cost. For a $200 session, that's $30–40. At medical spas with licensed medical staff performing the procedure, tipping is appreciated but less strictly expected — 10–15% is appropriate if you want to tip.
Do you tip at a medical spa for tattoo removal?
Tipping expectations are lower at medical spas than at tattoo studios. The procedure is performed by medical professionals in a clinical setting. A 10–15% tip is a thoughtful gesture, but not tipping is not considered rude in the way it would be at a salon.
Do you tip for every tattoo removal session?
Yes — tip at each individual session. Tattoo removal typically requires 6–12 sessions. Each session is a complete service, and the technician deserves recognition at each visit regardless of the overall treatment length.
Should you tip more for a large or complex tattoo removal?
Yes. Large tattoos, stubborn inks, or heavily layered areas require more passes and more careful technique. Tip toward the 20% end for these sessions, especially when the technician adjusts their approach for your specific ink.
How much should you tip for a package of tattoo removal sessions?
Tip at each visit on what one session costs you inside the package: the package price divided by its sessions. A $1,200 package of 8 sessions is $150 a session, so 15–20% is $23–30 per visit. Don't tip a percentage of the whole package up front.
Is tattoo removal tipping different from tattoo tipping?
Yes. Tattoo artists receive 20%+ tips routinely because tipping is deeply embedded in the tattoo industry. Tattoo removal technicians are tipped less consistently — 15–20% at studios, 10–15% at medical spas, and sometimes not at all at clinical settings.
What if you're unhappy with your tattoo removal progress?
Results depend heavily on ink type, skin, and immune response — factors outside the technician's control. Don't reduce your tip for slow fading unless the technique or aftercare guidance was genuinely poor. Tip based on service quality, not outcome pace.
